en: Being of advantage, beneficial.

advantageous.ety: From advantage + -ous or from Middle French avantageus (French avantageux). See advantage.

ex.ja: この結婚は彼の将来にとって有利になるだろう。

ex.en: The general situation is advantageous to us.
ex.ja: 全般的な状況はわれわれに有利だ。

ex.ja: 円高は我が社にとって好都合であった。

note.ja: advantage（有利）+ -ous。「有利な」。

Floating.

A group of many islands.

Excessively or extremely large or wealthy.

ex.ja: 当時の農家の暴利はすさまじかった。

ex.ja: 下腹部が張ります。

Dog-like.
Any member of Caninae, the only living subfamily of Canidae.
Any of certain extant canids regarded as similar to the dog or wolf (including coyotes, jackals, etc.) but distinguished from the vulpine…

canine.ety: From Latin canīnus (“of dogs, doglike, dogtooth”), from canis (“dog”). Compare French canin.

ex.en: I snapped the thread on my canine.
ex.ja: プチッ、と糸を犬歯で噛み切った。

note.ja: ラテン語 canis（犬）から。「犬の・犬歯」。canary と同じ。

en: Of, relating to, or being a cause of something; causing.
A word (such as because) that expresses a reason or a cause.

causal.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin causalis, from Latin causa (“cause”), equivalent to cause + -al, see cause.

note.ja: cause（原因）+ -al。「因果関係の」。casual（偶然の・気軽な）と綴りが似ているので注意。

en: A person, usually a young, attractive female, who encourages applause and cheers at a sports event, and wearing a specially-designed unif…
A person who rallies support for any cause.

ex.en: Ann is a cheerleader.
ex.ja: アンはチアガールです。

A stronghold or fortified place.

en: Lacking something essential; often construed with in.
Insufficient or inadequate in amount.
A person who is deficient.

deficient.ety: From Latin deficiens, present participle of deficere (“to lack, fail, be wanting”); see defect.

ex.en: The young engineer was deficient in experience.
ex.ja: その若い技師は経験が不足していた。

ex.en: My car is deficient in horsepower.
ex.ja: 私の車は馬力が足らない。

ex.ja: この建物は調和を欠いている。

en: Having deteriorated, degraded or fallen from normal, coherent, balanced and desirable to undesirable and typically abnormal.
Having lost good or desirable qualities; hence also having bad character or habits, base, immoral, corrupt.
One who is degenerate, who has fallen from previous stature; an immoral or corrupt person.
To lose good or desirable qualities.
To cause to lose good or desirable qualities.

degenerate.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin dēgenerātus. See -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.

note.ja: de（離れて）+ genus（種族）+ -ate。「本来の性質から外れる」→「退化する・堕落した」。gene と同じ gen。

en: Serving to deter, preventing something from happening.
Something that deters.

deterrent.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin dēterrēns, dēterrentem.

en: A feeling of contempt or scorn.
To regard (someone or something) with strong contempt.

disdain.ety: From Middle English disdeynen, from Old French desdeignier (modern French dédaigner).

ex.en: The soldier disdained shooting an unarmed enemy.
ex.ja: その兵士は丸腰の兵士を撃つことを潔しとしなかった。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ dignari（価値があると思う）。「価値がないと思う」→「軽蔑」。dignity と同じ。

en: Bringing or warranting disgrace; shameful.
Giving offense to moral sensibilities and injurious to reputation.

ex.en: She was too proud to do anything disgraceful.
ex.ja: 彼女はプライドが高いので恥ずべきことはしなかった。

note.ja: disgrace（不名誉）+ -ful。「恥ずべき」。

en: Inspiring fear, especially in a mysterious or shadowy way; strange, weird.
Frightened, timid.
An eerie creature or thing.

eerie.ety: From Middle English eri (“fearful”), from Old English earg (“cowardly, fearful”), from Proto-West Germanic *arg, from Proto-Germanic *argaz. Akin to Scots ergh, argh from the same Old English source. Doublet of argh.

ex.en: The eerie silence struck terror into their hearts.
ex.ja: 無気味な静けさが彼らの心胆を寒からしめた。

ex.en: One image comes to mind: an eerie, pitch-black disk.
ex.ja: 頭の中に一つのイメージが湧きあがる。不気味で真っ黒な円盤。

note.ja: 古英語 earg（臆病な）から。スコットランド英語で「怖がりの」→「不気味な」。

en: Angered, made furious, made full of rage.

enraged.ety: Inherited from Middle English [Term?]. By surface analysis, enrage + -ed.

ex.en: The members of the opposition party were enraged against the bill.
ex.ja: 反対党議員はその法案に激怒した。

ex.en: Don't you know he is enraged at your insult?
ex.ja: 彼が君の侮辱を受けて怒っているのをしらないのか。

ex.ja: ＳＥが辞め続けると会社の競争力が落ちる。

en: A brief recreational trip; a journey out of the usual way.
A field trip.
To go on a recreational trip or excursion.

excursion.ety: Borrowed from Latin excursiō (“a running out, an inroad, invasion, a setting out, beginning of a speech”), from excurrere (“to run out”), from ex (“out”) + currere (“to run”). By surface analysis, excurse + -ion. Compare excursus.

ex.en: I am looking forward very much to the school excursion.
ex.ja: 私は修学旅行を大変楽しみにしている。

ex.en: Our class went on an excursion to Hakone.
ex.ja: 私たちのクラスは箱根へ遠足に行った。

ex.en: All in all, the excursion was pleasant.
ex.ja: 全体として、遠足は楽しかった。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ curs（走る）+ ion。外へ走り出ること →「遠足・小旅行」。

en: A style of humor marked by broad improbabilities with little regard to regularity or method.
A motion picture or play featuring this style of humor.
To stuff with forcemeat or other food items.
To fill full; to stuff.

farce.ety: Borrowed from Middle French farce (“farce (style of humor); stuffing”) (in the latter sense, via Middle English fars, farsse), from Old French farse, from Medieval Latin farsa, from the feminine perfect passive participle of Latin farciō (“to stuff”). ex.ja: だが、レーガン政権と最高裁判所に潰される前でさえ、ＯＳＨＡは茶番であった。

note.ja: フランス語 farce（詰め物）から。ラテン語 farcire（詰める）。劇の合間に詰め込んだ道化芝居 →「茶番・笑劇」。

An act of moving the limbs or body with violent movements, especially in a dance.
To throw with violence or quick movement; to hurl.
To move (oneself) abruptly or violently; to rush or dash.

fling.ety: From Middle English fling, from the verb (see below). Compare Icelandic flengur (“a fast sprint”).

ex.ja: 敵は新兵力を投入した。

en: In a state of panic, worry, frenzy, or rush.
Extremely energetic.

frantic.ety: From Middle English frantike, frentik, variant of frenetik, from Old French frenetique, from Late Latin phreneticus, alteration of phreniticus, from φρενιτικός (phrenitikós, “mad, suffering from inflammation of the brain”), from φρενῖτις (phrenîtis, “inflammation of the brain”), from φρήν (phrḗn, “the brain”). ex.en: You did a lot of work in frantic haste.
ex.ja: あなたはたくさんの仕事を狂わんばかりに急いで片づけた。

en: A type of very sweet candy or confection, usually made from sugar, butter, and milk or cream.
Chocolate fudge.
To try to avoid giving a direct answer.
To alter something from its true state, as to hide a flaw or uncertainty, deliberately but not necessarily dishonestly or immorally.
Used in place of fuck.

fudge.ety: Probably a variant of fadge (“to fit”), the confectionery sense having evolved from the meaning of “merging together” or “turning out as expected”.

ex.en: Fudge! My stocking's run.
ex.ja: やだストッキング伝線しちゃってる。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「ごまかす」→ 失敗して偶然できた菓子 →「ファッジ」。

en: To move softly, smoothly, or effortlessly.
To fly unpowered, as of an aircraft. Also relates to gliding birds and flying fish.
The act of gliding.
A transitional sound, especially a semivowel.

glide.ety:
From Middle English gliden, from Old English glīdan, from Proto-West Germanic *glīdan, from Proto-Germanic *glīdaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰleydʰ-.
Cognate with West Frisian glide, glydzje, Low German glieden, Dutch glijden, German gleiten, Norwegian Nynorsk gli, Danish glide, Swedish glida, Finnish liitää.

ex.ja: ハンググライダーに興味を持ったきっかけは何ですか？

ex.en: Do you consider hang gliding dangerous?
ex.ja: あなたはハンググライディングが危険だと思いますか？

ex.en: The white yacht was gliding over the sea.
ex.ja: 白いヨットが海面を滑るように走っていた。

note.ja: 古英語 glīdan（滑る）から。「滑るように進む・滑空する」。glider。

en: To cause sorrow or distress to.
To feel very sad about; to mourn; to sorrow for.
A manager or steward, e.g. of a farm.

grieve.ety:

For the meaning development compare Russian тяготи́ть (tjagotítʹ, “to be a burden (on), to oppress”), Russian тужи́ть (tužítʹ, “to experience grief”), related to тяжёлый (tjažólyj, “heavy, grave”), тя́жкий (tjážkij).

ex.ja: 彼の死は惜しんでも余りあるものだ。

ex.ja: 彼は親友の死を嘆き悲しんだ。

ex.ja: 彼女は十年近くも彼の死を嘆き悲しんでいる。

ex.ja: トムは根に持つタイプではない。

ex.en: I am grudged even the least bit of happiness.
ex.ja: ほんのひとかけらの幸せさえ私には許されない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 grouchier（不平を言う）から。grouch（不平家）と同じ。「恨み」。

ex.ja: その髪型が瞬く間に若者の間に広まった。

heartless.ety: From Middle English hertles, herteles, from Old English heortlēas (“without courage; listless”), equivalent to heart + -less. Cognate with German herzlos.

ex.ja: そんなことを言うなんて彼はつれない。

ex.ja: 俺はあんな血も涙もない人間じゃないぞ。

ex.ja: あいつは思いやりがない。

note.ja: heart（心）+ -less。「心がない」→「無情な」。

en: Very busy with activity and confusion.

ex.ja: 彼は慌ただしい毎日を送っています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hektikos（習慣的な・消耗性の）から。消耗熱の「熱っぽい」→「てんてこ舞いの」。

en: The point that stands backward in an arrow, fishhook, etc., to prevent it from being easily extracted. Hence: Anything which stands out w…
A hurtful or disparaging remark.
To furnish with barbs, or with that which will hold or hurt like barbs, as an arrow, fishhook, spear, etc.
To cut (hair).

barb.ety:
PIE word
 *bʰardʰéh₂
From Middle English barbe, from Middle French barbe, from Old French barbe (“beard, beard-like element”). Doublet of beard.

note.ja: ラテン語 barba（ひげ）から。「ひげのようなとげ」→「（釣り針の）かえし・とげのある言葉」。barber と同じ。

en: A projecting part of a rampart or other fortification.
A well-fortified position; a stronghold or citadel.
To furnish with a bastion.

bastion.ety: First attested in 1562. From French bastion, from Old French bastille (“fortress”).

note.ja: イタリア語 bastione（大きな砦）から。bastire（築く）。「砦・拠点」。

en: A large cushion or pillow, usually cylindrical in shape.
A pad, quilt, or anything used to hinder pressure, support part of the body, or make a bandage sit easy upon a wounded part; a compress.
To brace, reinforce, secure, or support.

bolster.ety: From Middle English bolster, bolstre, from Old English bolster (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *bolstr, from Proto-Germanic *bulstraz (“pillow, cushion”). Cognate with Scots bowster (“bolster”), West Frisian bulster (“mattress”), Dutch bolster (“husk, shell”), German Polster (“bolster, pillow, pad”), Swedish bolster (“soft mattress, bolster”), Icelandic bólstur (“pillow”).

note.ja: 古英語 bolster（長枕）から。「長枕」→ 支える →「強化する」。

en: A small fighting force specially trained for making quick destructive raids against enemy-held areas.
A commando trooper.

commando.ety: From Afrikaans kommando, from Portuguese comando (“command”), from Late Latin *commandare, from Latin commendare.

note.ja: com（強く）+ mand（命じる）+ o。ポルトガル語 comando（命令→部隊）から →「奇襲部隊（員）・コマンドー」。

ja: 居心地のよい（英国のつづり）

en: Affording comfort and warmth; snug; social and comfortable.
Warm and comfortable.
A padded or knit covering put on an item to keep it warm, especially a teapot or egg.
A padded or knit covering for any item (often an electronic device such as a laptop computer).
To become snug and comfortable.
To become friendly with.

cosy.ety: From Scots cosie, from Old Scots colsie, but ultimate derivation is unknown. Possibly of North Germanic origin, such as Norwegian kose seg (“to have a cozy time”), from Old Norse kose sig, from koselig, koslig, perhaps ultimately from Old High German kōsa; see modern German kosen (“to cuddle”).

ex.en: Your house has a very cozy atmosphere.
ex.ja: あなたの家はとても居心地のよい雰囲気ですね。

ex.en: He lives in a little cozy house.
ex.ja: 彼は住み心地がよい小さな家に住んでいます。

ex.en: He lives in a cozy little house.
ex.ja: 彼は住み心地がよい小さな家に住んでいます。

note.ja: cozy のイギリスのつづり。スコットランド語に由来する。

en: A line or mark made by folding or doubling any pliable substance; hence, a similar mark, however produced.
One of the white lines drawn on the pitch to show different areas of play; especially the popping crease, but also the bowling crease and…
To make a crease in; to wrinkle.
To undergo creasing; to form wrinkles.

crease.ety: From earlier English creast, from Middle English crest (“ridge, crest”). More at crest.

ex.en: This dress creases easily.
ex.ja: この服はすぐしわになる。

note.ja: crest（とさか）の変化形とされる。「折り目・しわ」。

en: The act or process of removing water from something.
The condition in which water in the body drops below normal levels, usually caused by illness, sweating or by not drinking enough.

dehydration.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *de
Proto-Indo-European *-h₁
Proto-Indo-European *déh₁
Proto-Italic *dē
Latin dē
Latin dē-der.
English de-
English hydration
English dehydration
From de- + hydration.

ex.en: "How is it?" "Well, yes ... could be some signs of dehydration."
ex.ja: 「具合はどうなんですか？」「ああ、うん・・・少し脱水症状が出ているかな」

ex.en: The doctor told me to drink more water to prevent dehydration.
ex.ja: お医者さんに、脱水症状の予防のためにもっと水を飲みなさないと言われました。

ex.en: For dehydration, take a lick of salt.
ex.ja: 脱水症状には、塩をひと舐め。

note.ja: de（取り除く）+ hydrate（水を与える）+ -ion。ギリシャ語 hydōr（水）。「脱水」。

en: The act of naming or designating.
That by which anything is denominated or styled; an epithet; a name, designation, or title; especially, a general name indicating a class…

denomination.ety: From Middle English denominacioun, from Old French denominacion, from Latin dēnōminātiō. By surface analysis, denominate + -ion.

note.ja: de（完全に）+ nomin（名前）+ ation。名をつけること →「宗派・（貨幣の）単位・名称」。

en: The process, in the gastrointestinal tract, by which food is converted into substances that can be used by the body.
The result of this process.

digestion.ety: From Old French digestion. Partly displaced native Old English melting (“melting, digestion”).

ex.en: A natural diet is suitable for human digestion.
ex.ja: 自然食は人間の消化に合っている。

ex.en: Natural food is not always good for our digestion.
ex.ja: 自然食品がつねに消化にいいとは限らない。

note.ja: digest（消化する）+ -ion。di + gerere（運ぶ）。「消化」。
